title: The New Development Bank Quietly Delivers During India’s BRICS Year
gist: With India chairing BRICS and hosting the September 2026 New Delhi summit, the author argues the New Development Bank is the clearest evidence BRICS produces concrete output beyond summit statements. He proposes judging it on disbursement, borrower mix and funding sources, and says on all three it looks better than its low profile suggests.

themes.theme: NDB as proof of BRICS substance

insights.claim: The New Development Bank is the clearest evidence that BRICS produces something beyond summit statements, a question that resurfaced as India hosted the BRICS summit in New Delhi in September 2026.
insights.so_what: Investors judging BRICS as a policy bloc should track NDB lending, not communiqués, as the concrete signal of institutional traction for non-Western development finance.
insights.quote: The New Development Bank (NDB) offers the clearest evidence in the affirmative.
insights.locator: As India hosted the BRICS summit
insights.speaker: Sachin Yadav

insights.claim: The NDB's record is more encouraging than its low public profile suggests across lending volume and disbursement, borrower mix, and how it raises funds.
insights.so_what: Market perception of the Shanghai-headquartered NDB may understate its operational scale, relevant for its bond issuance and for alternative development-finance channels.
insights.quote: On all three, the picture is more encouraging than the NDB’s low public profile suggests.
insights.locator: As India hosted the BRICS summit
insights.speaker: Sachin Yadav

insights.claim: India first proposed the New Development Bank at a 2012 BRICS summit in New Delhi, so its 2026 BRICS chairship brought the idea full circle.
insights.so_what: India has political ownership of the NDB, which may make it a champion of the bank's expansion during its chairship.
insights.locator: As India hosted the BRICS summit
insights.speaker: Sachin Yadav

themes.theme: How to evaluate a development bank

insights.claim: A development bank should be judged on money that actually reaches projects rather than big announcements, specifically on: how much it has lent and disbursed, whom it lends to, and how it raises the money it lends.
insights.so_what: A disbursement-vs-commitment lens is a useful filter for any multilateral lender's headlines, separating pledges from real capital deployment.
insights.quote: big announcements matter less than the money that actually reaches projects
insights.locator: As India hosted the BRICS summit
insights.speaker: Sachin Yadav
